A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 12 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Sections A–B, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original patch-level and region-level experiments on ATD, GenAI, and PBC, including training-scale ablations and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and A–D and the accompanying figures.

M1.justification: The ViT and Multiplex Transformer, sampled contrastive loss, automatic annotation pipeline, edge-aware patch merging, and bidirectional region matching are unchanged. Revised explanatory wording does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same in-house anime training data, ATD and GenAI evaluation datasets, and supplementary PBC training and evaluation. Shortening the dataset discussion does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: Dai et al.'s adapted framework with TrappedBall remains the quantitative baseline; ClosedRegion and SAM remain in the qualitative comparisons. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Training settings, preprocessing, metrics, and evaluation procedures are retained, including 25 ATD and 40 GenAI test pairs, the PBC split, 20 training epochs, and the region-pair purity threshold above 0.8.

E4.justification: The 20k/100k/200k training-scale ablation remains in Figure 5 and Tables A–B, and the qualitative analyses remain unchanged. Removing a sentence directing readers to supplementary tables does not remove those results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative results match throughout Tables 1–2 and A–D and the figures. For example, the proposed method's region accuracies remain 84.44% on ATD, 78.43% on GenAI, and 59.92% on PBC.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), correspondence definitions, similarity construction, and matching rules are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same task novelty, Transformer framework, annotation-pipeline contribution, and performance claims.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the explanation of ATD/GenAI differences, low region recall, loss of small semantic details during merging, and the PBC segmentation–recall trade-off. Revised prior-work and baseline framing does not introduce a new results analysis.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page footnote stating that the dataset and code are available and supplies a repository link; v3 only promises a future release in Section 4.2. Implementation details remain unchanged, and repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to The Animation Transformer, Feng et al.'s industrial cel-animation colorization framework, and Matcha. Sections 2.2 and 5.2 refine the contrast with segmentation-dependent prior methods and characterize the retained baseline as among the strongest reproducible pipelines.

P1.justification: Localized edits condense Sections 2.1 and 5.1, rewrite related-work and baseline passages, and replace 'token features' with 'patch-level features.' Author affiliation, contact information, and footnotes change; the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The added contact line and resource footnote shift the first-page abstract and Figure 1, while text and references reflow locally. Figures, plots, table structures, and captions retain their content and design; printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: v4 supplies a concrete code/data access pointer where v3 only promised release and modestly broadens acknowledgment of relevant prior work. These improve reproducibility documentation and context. The empirical evidence is unchanged, so the stronger baseline characterization gains no additional experimental support; repository contents also remain unverifiable from the PDFs.
